cells.tense: You're in the middle of your practice and what's in front of you comes through plain, without any dressing on it.
cells.ask: Once today, write down one plain fact about something you've been working on, with no verdict attached.
cells.core:
There's a moment in the work where you just see it — no commentary, no fixing, no deciding whether it's any good. That moment is the whole practice, and you're in it. A small lamp on a bench, kept lit by your showing up rather than by anything flashy: that's what this looks like when it's going well, and it's going well.

The plainness is the point. What it can feed next is the same bare looking carried into the next thing you pick up — a look that doesn't check itself against how it'll land. You can go a little further today, not to prove anything, just because the clear look is already here and doesn't need a reason.
cells.sheetLine: What's there comes through plain, and you don't add anything to it.
cells.verb: seeing what's actually there, before naming it
cells.place: in the quiet practice you keep at, alone, a little at a time

cells.tense: You're bracing for how the work will look once you've got it right, and that's pulling you off what's actually in front of you.
cells.ask: Before your next practice session, sit with nothing for two minutes — then start with no plan for the outcome.
cells.core:
You know the feeling: you're looking at something and already thinking about how you'll improve it, what you'll say about it, what it should become. The practice turns into a rehearsal for a finished result that hasn't arrived, and the pressure to get it right takes over. That doesn't sharpen anything — it narrows what you can take in to what you've already decided. Your own looking gets lost under the projected outcome.

The bench is still there, and one honest look at what's on it would settle you fast. There's a different way to be here, and it's available right now. Before you sit down, prepare nothing. Two minutes just being with the materials, no goal, no standard. Let this moment be the first one. The finish takes care of itself once you've seen plainly what's already there — and that only happens when you stop running ahead of it.
cells.sheetLine: You're trying to see the finished thing instead of what's in front of you.
cells.verb: seeing what's actually there, before naming it
cells.place: in the quiet practice you keep at, alone, a little at a time

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's behind you — the moment to take in what was there came and went, and the practice has gone quiet.
cells.ask: Today, give five uninterrupted minutes to one piece of your practice, and write down what you notice in it — no editing.
cells.core:
The practice has been running on empty. You set it down, and things move through without you really catching them. It isn't that you can't see — you can — but something in you has stopped putting your attention on the line. The small steady light is still there; it's just not getting fed.

When this is fed, it looks like a workbench with one lamp on it and nothing rushing: you sit, you look, you write a line. It comes back by doing, not by deciding to feel motivated. One session, five minutes, one thing you notice written down. The note isn't the point — the point is that when you put your hand to this, the looking returns on its own. Worth checking: is there a piece of the practice you can touch today, even a small one?
cells.sheetLine: The looking is still here. It's the showing up that stopped.
cells.verb: seeing what's actually there, before naming it
cells.place: in the quiet practice you keep at, alone, a little at a time

cells.tense: You're writing in a room you're already in — the practice is happening, but you talk about it as if it runs itself.
cells.ask: Name one thing you saw today that you didn't plan to see, and say 'I noticed that.'
cells.core:
A bench, a lamp, five minutes, one plain note about what's in front of you: that's what this looks like when it's working, and it's working. You already practice. You already notice. But when you talk about it, it sounds like something that happens to you — the right idea showing up, the clear moment arriving, as if someone else sat down and put the attention there. You're the one who did that, and you move past it before any of it counts as yours.

One thing you saw today that you didn't plan to see, named in a sentence. When you let yourself be the one who looked, even quietly, the practice holds steadier. Try it now, one line, before the moment goes.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one who did the looking. Nothing else needs saying.
cells.verb: seeing what's actually there, before naming it
cells.place: in the quiet practice you keep at, alone, a little at a time
